<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Messages to a seat in a long turn wait for that turn to end. Today that cost hours (F25). This plan measures the wait per message, has the PA flag waits over 15 minutes, adds `--urgent` for the few messages a working seat must see now (Copilot through onPostToolUse; OMP/Pi already steer; others downgrade with a reason), and makes s12 limits count from delivery (F73), and a reply with --in-reply-to answers a request (F68, moved from plan 212's follow-ups). Owner: delivery (pij-swift-kestrel). Order (prime, 23:25): 214 comes before any further 212 work; it is the biggest drag on the fleet's speed.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Measure how long messages wait behind a busy turn, flag long holds to the PA, add an --urgent send that lands at the next tool boundary, and start role-request limits at delivery.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Changing FYI semantics or the cold-wake rule.
- Any new delivery timer or poll.

<a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

F25 measured (pm-001, live store, 6 Nov 2026, jobs.enqueued_at to jobs.acked_at for kind delivery:*): 152 of 1,364 deliveries were held over 15 min. pij-local-warbler: 39 of 52 over 15 min, 25 over an hour, max 7.5 h; pij-back-tapir 31 of 48 (max 4 h); pij-swift-kestrel 29 of 38 (max 4 h); pij-wary-lynx 20 of 47 (max 3 h). pm-001's 13:38 to 18:44 sends to warbler reached it between 22:36 and 23:18. That is why #130 needed three asks, and it caused both performance reworks and kestrel's slip. Seams: the daemon queues to Copilot seats with reason extension-stream (crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs, enqueue_carrier); the Copilot extension (.copilot/extensions/pij/extension.mjs) only has onUserPromptSubmitted today, which carries held FYIs. The Copilot SDK (copilot-sdk/types.d.ts) has onPostToolUse and onPostToolUseFailure, whose `additionalContext` the host appends as guidance to the model. OMP/Pi already deliver with deliverAs: steer (.omp/extensions/pij/adapters/pi-runtime.ts). Claude delivery is crates/transport/src/uds.rs. F73 (warbler, 23:19): request 01a1b0ab had a 20 min limit, reached warbler at 23:18:55, was answered at 23:18:59 with --in-reply-to, and the check-in still fired at 23:19:16 because the clock ran from creation.

<a id="open-questions"></a>

## Open Questions

| question | state | note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does jobs.acked_at mark the body reaching the session for every rung, or only the daemon handing it to a stream? The answer decides whether AC1 needs a migration. | [x] checked | Answered: yes. Every rung acks the delivery job after the body reaches the session (the Copilot extension acks after the host consumes the steered prompt; OMP/Pi after the steer; PTY/UDS after injection), so acked_at - enqueued_at is the held time. Live store, 24 h: the whole hold is enqueued_at to claimed_at; acked_at - claimed_at is 0 for every Copilot seat. No migration for AC1; migration 0038 only remembers which long holds the digest has shown. |
| Should urgent sends be rate-capped per sender? Proposed: no cap at first; the spine event and the PA's per-sender count make abuse visible. | [x] checked | Answered: no cap. The send.urgent spine event (one per urgent send, with sender) makes overuse visible to the PA. |
| Can the Claude socket path reach a running turn, or is Claude a downgrade for now? | [x] checked | Answered: the Claude socket transport already delivers between tool calls mid-turn (crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs, the transport-judges-busy comment), so urgent to a socket Claude seat changes nothing (outcome injected); a Claude seat without the socket downgrades. |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
- Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
- No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
- Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
- One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
